correctness.rationale: A complete analytic proof identifies allowed acyclic sign arrays, evaluates all same-path and cross-path signed products by exact finite combinatorics, and pushes their covariance through telescoping incidence matrices. Global reversal yields mean zero. The exact universal formula was independently reproduced by an integer checker for eight bounded instances with three to six paths and unequal lengths, with all matrix entries equal; the proof, not enumeration, supplies the infinite statement.

Another related covariance theorem is confined to cactus graphs; generalized theta graphs have overlapping cycles. value.rationale: The complete uniform-vertex covariance is a geometrically motivated invariant, yielding all Euclidean second moments and mean squared vertex separation. It treats arbitrary many unequal paths with overlapping cycles, where known direct-sum cactus formulas do not apply. The theorem isolates a nonzero rank-one terminal correction and positive pathwise Laplacian reweightings; its sharp equal-three-path distance asymptotic exhibits nontrivial quantitative geometry rather than a routine reparametrization.
